sections.label: HDB Bill amendments overview
sections.summary: The passage lists four changes: MAS liquidity use of security interests, compulsory acquisition for false statements, standardised compensation forum, and HDB Board appointments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, it will allow approved financial institutions to use their security interest in property loans involving HDB flats as security for liquidity from the Monetary Authority of Singapore or MAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, it will enable compulsory acquisition action to be taken, as a measure of last resort, against flat owners who deliberately make misleading or false statements, or misrepresent a material fact, when transferring a flat between related persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, it will standardise the forum in Court to which HDB applies to deposit compensation related to compulsory acquisition, or to deposit compensation when the flat is vested in HDB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Fourth, it will enhance HDB's ability to manage its Board appointments.

sections.label: Compensation deposit forum change
sections.summary: Clause 5 moves the forum for HDB to deposit compensation on a flat's vesting from the High Court to the Registrar of the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 5 changes the judicial forum to which HDB applies to deposit compensation related to the vesting of a flat on the demise of the owner, from the High Court to the Registrar of the Supreme Court.

sections.label: HDB Board size increase
sections.summary: Clause 2 raises the maximum number of HDB Board members from 12 to 15 to bring in additional expertise and perspectives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: HDB sees the need for more diverse views, experience, and skillsets on its Board to guide its efforts in providing even better-quality homes and continuing to enhance the HDB living environment in a financially sustainable manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These efforts will benefit from fresh insights, for example, in the areas of new technology that can help us develop greener, smarter, and more sustainable towns, and in the area of healthcare and ageing issues to guide our efforts to provide a quality living environment for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill therefore increases the maximum number of Board members to 15, up from 12 currently, to allow HDB more room to bring in additional expertise and new perspectives to complement the existing Board.

sections.label: Board quorum and MAS Facility
sections.summary: The amendments update Board meeting quorum to one-third of members in office, and a new MAS Singapore dollar Term Facility is mentioned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, the amendments will update the quorum for Board meetings to one-third of the total number of Board Members in office.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: For MAS to establish a new Singapore dollar Term Facility to provide liquidity to local banks in Singapore through inclusion of a wider range of collaterals, this would be a welcome move.

sections.label: Financial controls on Facility
sections.summary: The passage asks what financial controls will ensure extended liquidity flows to local businesses rather than banks' overseas portfolio investments.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given that the intent is to assist local businesses in obtaining greater liquidity, what financial controls on the Facility will be in place to ensure the extended liquidity will be flowed to local businesses instead of investments that are related to the banks' overseas portfolio?

sections.label: Questions on Board and acquisition
sections.summary: The passage asks the rationale for increasing Board members, exploring alternatives, and including compulsory acquisition for false declarations, noting HDB residency figures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: One, what is the rationale to increase the number of Board Members instead of reviewing the role and the scope of the existing Board?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The next is, before the decision to increase the number of board members, were other alternatives explored such as seeking external consultants and industry experts for advice on an ongoing basis rather than to formalise this expertise within the Board members?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: And the final area, in response to the greater empowerment of HDB to compulsorily acquire a flat, under the fact that there is a false or misleading declaration, I would like to know, since Minister has said the chances of this misrepresentation or even false declaration is very low, then what is the rationale for including this in the amendment, in the terms of HDB flats and private properties, since it is going to be very low in this perspective?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, more than 80% of Singapore's resident population resides in HDB flats, while homeownership rates among resident households for HDB dwellings is high at 92%.

sections.label: Deputy Chairman role made discretionary
sections.summary: The amendment proposes making the Deputy Chairman of the Board role discretionary instead of mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The amendment proposes to make the role of Deputy Chairman of the Board discretionary rather than mandatory.

sections.label: Compulsory acquisition for false statements
sections.summary: The paragraph adds reasons for compulsory property acquisition where an owner made a misleading or false statement in a Board application, and asks how many such related-party transactions occurred and whether HDB suffered damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The paragraph extends the list of possible reasons for the compulsory acquisition of a property if the owner has made a misleading or false statement in his application to the Board for his acquisition or transfer of interest of a flat from or to a related party respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How many of such transactions took place and did the HDB suffer damages as a result of these transactions between related persons?

sections.label: Bank collateral and flat seizure powers
sections.summary: It enables banks to use HDB loans as collateral to borrow from MAS, and empowers HDB to seize flats where homeowners provide falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, it enables banks to use HDB loans as collaterals to borrow from MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, it empowers the HDB to seize flats in certain cases where homeowners provide falsehoods to HDB.

sections.label: Extension of late payment charge suspension
sections.summary: The Minister announced that given current economic conditions, HDB will further extend the suspension of late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears to 31 March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I was initially going to ask if HDB will continue to suspend late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad the Minister has announced that given the current economic conditions, HDB will further extend this to 31 March 2021.

sections.label: HDB power over false applications
sections.summary: HDB now has power to act where applications for flat ownership in an acquisition or transfer between relatives contained a false or misleading statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In particular, HDB now has the power to do so in cases where applications for flat ownerships in an acquisition or transfer between relatives contained a false or misleading statement.

sections.label: Mortgage and rental rebate measures
sections.summary: Examples given are the suspension of late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears till March 2021 and a 50% rental rebate for public rental flat households from 1 October to 31 December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, the suspension of late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears till March 2021; and that households living in public rental flats will receive a 50% rental rebate between 1 October and 31 December 2020.

sections.label: HDB mortgages as bank collateral
sections.summary: A Bill amendment aims to let domestic banks use HDB mortgages as collateral for an MAS facility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the amendments in this Bill aims to allow our domestic banks to use HDB mortgages as collateral for a grant of facility from MAS.

sections.label: MAS ESG loan facility
sections.summary: The MAS Singapore Dollar Facility for ESG Loans gives banks and finance companies credit at 0.1% interest per annum for SME credit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, the MAS Singapore Dollar Facility for ESG Loans provides a line of credit to our banks and finance companies at 0.1% interest per annum, to ensure vital credit for our SMEs during these difficult times.

sections.label: Compulsory acquisition for misleading statements
sections.summary: The Bill adds a ground for HDB compulsory acquisition where an owner made a misleading statement or misrepresentation of material fact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I turn now to the second point I would like to make about this Bill – compulsory acquisition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Bill also intends to add in a further ground for HDB to take compulsory acquisition, or CA action, of a HDB flat if the owner of that flat and I quote – "... made a misleading statement in his application  , or a misrepresentation of a material fact (whether innocently or otherwise)" in relation to the acquisition of that flat or an interest in that flat, or in the transfer of an interest in that flat to a related person.

sections.label: Consequences of compulsory acquisition
sections.summary: Compulsory acquisition means HDB-decided compensation and possible effects on future flat applications and concessionary loans, applying section 56 to sole or multi-owner purchases or transfers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The consequences of a CA action are understandably severe: (a) in accordance with HDB's compensation policy, owners of a flat subject to CA action will obtain compensation decided by the HDB; and (b) their future applications for a flat may be affected if they have used up their allocated number of HDB concessionary loans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, this amendment will apply section 56 to purchases or transfers – to acquisitions or transfers of interests in a flat in both a sole, or a multi-owner situation.

sections.label: Innocent co-owners and concessionary loans
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether innocent co-owners will be prejudiced in future flat applications and suggests allowing them another HDB concessionary loan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Or will these innocent co-owners be prejudiced by the compulsory acquisition in any future applications for another HDB flat?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It would help if innocent co-owners are allowed another HDB concessionary loan if they had used up their entitled HDB concessionary loans for the previous flat which was subject to CA action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe some clarity on how innocent HDB owners will be treated will assure many of us.

sections.label: Facility during COVID-19 crisis
sections.summary: The facility will remain in place throughout the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The facility will remain in place throughout the COVID-19 crisis.

sections.label: Housing non-performing loan ratio
sections.summary: The current housing non-performing loan ratio remains low and stable at around 0.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The current housing non-performing loan ratio remains low and stable at around 0.5%.

sections.label: Support for borrowers in difficulty
sections.summary: MAS worked with financial institutions on support measures giving borrowers in financial difficulties more time to resume monthly mortgage instalments, announced yesterday, easing cashflow and encouraging repayment in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For borrowers in financial difficulties, MAS has worked with financial institutions on further support measures that allow them more time to resume their monthly mortgage instalments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These measures, which were announced yesterday, will help ease individuals’ cashflow while gradually encouraging them to resume their home loan repayments in 2021.

sections.label: HDB false statement cases
sections.summary: HDB found around 10 such cases in the past three years, mainly false statements or misrepresentations about eligibility and property ownership, making this a pre-emptive move to deter potential infringements in flat ownership transfers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, HDB had found around 10 such cases in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They principally revolve around false statements or misrepresentations about eligibility, about ownership of other properties, both locally and abroad and, of course, other statements that are material to the transfer or to purchase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is thus a pre-emptive move to deter any such potential infringements in relation to the transfer of flat ownership.

sections.label: Section 56 amendment terms
sections.summary: For the purposes of the section 56 amendment, the ordinary meaning of the terms "acquisition" and "transfer" should be taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For the purposes of section 56 amendment, we should take the ordinary meaning of the terms "acquisition" and "transfer".

sections.label: HDB Board size expansion
sections.summary: With the expansion, HDB's Board size will be comparable to that of other Statutory Boards such as the LTA, CPF Board and JTC Corporation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: With the expansion, HDB’s Board size will be comparable to that of other Statutory Boards such as the LTA, CPF Board and JTC Corporation.
